mfa_enforced_for_admin.title: MFA Enforced for All Admin Logins
mfa_enforced_for_admin.description: Attestation: every administrative/privileged login is gated by multi-factor authentication (not a password alone), enforced via the IdP/SSO directory with no admin-role exclusions (CIS 6.5, NIST AC). Secure = true. The exposure fires when MFA is NOT enforced for admins (false), leaving privileged logins password-only and a stolen admin password alone yields a valid session — the primary enabler of credential stuffing, phishing, and valid-credential abuse.

phishing_resistant_authenticator_require.title: Phishing-Resistant Authenticator Required
phishing_resistant_authenticator_require.description: Attestation: the admin MFA factor is phishing-resistant (FIDO2/WebAuthn or PKI/PIV, origin-bound, AAL2/AAL3 per NIST SP 800-63B / CISA) rather than a phishable shared-secret factor (SMS, voice, TOTP, push). Secure value = fido2_or_piv. The exposure fires on the insecure value sms_otp_or_push, which an AiTM proxy defeats by relaying the captured OTP/push approval to mint a valid session.

admin_credential_hygiene.title: Admin Credential Hygiene Enforced
admin_credential_hygiene.description: Attestation: the residual password factor for admin accounts is strong, unique, and screened against breached-password datasets, with lockout/throttling bound to the account (CIS 5.2, OWASP Credential Stuffing). Secure = true. As a secondary trigger the exposure fires when hygiene is NOT attested (false): reused/short/breached admin passwords make the password leg stuffable even where MFA exists.

no_shared_privileged_credentials.title: Privileged Actions Attributable to Named Operators
no_shared_privileged_credentials.description: Attestation: every privileged action is attributable to one named human operator — no shared/generic admin logins in routine use (NIST AC-2(7), CIS 5.1). Secure = true. The exposure fires when false — a shared credential broadens who can present 'valid' credentials and makes privileged actions non-attributable even when a log exists, defeating identity-level incident response.

privileged_session_anomaly_monitoring.title: Privileged Session Anomaly Monitoring
privileged_session_anomaly_monitoring.description: Attestation: privileged accounts are monitored for atypical usage (off-hours login, impossible travel, atypical resource access) so abuse of valid admin credentials is detected (NIST AC-2(12), MITRE T1078 detection). Secure = true. The exposure fires when false — an adversary using stolen valid credentials blends into normal traffic undetected.

no_standing_admin_privileges_jit_require.title: No Standing Privilege — JIT Elevation Required
no_standing_admin_privileges_jit_require.description: Attestation: privileged access is just-in-time (requested, justified, approved, time-bounded, auto-revoked) toward Zero Standing Privileges, rather than standing/always-on admin role assignments. Secure = true (JIT/ZSP brokered, no persistent active privileged role). The exposure fires when false — always-on standing admin rights an attacker can ride for lateral movement after a single foothold (BeyondTrust ZSP; Entra PIM eligible-vs-active).

least_privilege_admin_scoping.title: Least-Privilege Admin Scoping
least_privilege_admin_scoping.description: Attestation: each admin holds only the minimum privileges required for their role via documented RBAC, rather than blanket global-admin / root-everywhere. Secure = true (scoped least-privilege roles, CIS 6.8; NIST AC-6 / AC-6(5)). The exposure fires when false — over-broad superuser scope that lets a compromised operator pivot across the whole trust zone.

privileged_access_via_pam_with_session_r.title: Privileged Access Brokered Through PAM with Session Recording
privileged_access_via_pam_with_session_r.description: Attestation: privileged access is brokered through a PAM/bastion that vaults credentials and records sessions, so operators do not hold raw long-lived secrets and access is centrally monitored (NIST AC-2(7); OpenSSH bastion hardening). Secure = true. The exposure fires when false — operators connect directly with raw credentials and sessions are unvaulted/unrecorded, widening the lateral-movement surface.

periodic_privilege_recertification.title: Periodic Privilege Recertification
periodic_privilege_recertification.description: Attestation: privileged entitlements are reviewed on a defined recurring frequency and excess/stale rights are reassigned or removed (NIST AC-6(7); CIS 5.1 inventory-driven recertification). Secure = true. The exposure fires when false (no recurring privilege review) — entitlements accumulate as unreviewed standing access (privilege creep).

dormant_admin_accounts_disabled.title: Dormant Admin Accounts Disabled
dormant_admin_accounts_disabled.description: Attestation: unused/dormant privileged accounts are disabled or removed within a defined window (CIS 5.3: 45 days; NIST AC-2(3)) and admin access is revoked promptly on termination/role change (CIS 6.2). Secure = true. The exposure fires when false — terminated or role-changed operators retain admin access and dormant privileged accounts linger as quiet footholds for re-entry.

shared_admin_accounts.title: Shared Admin Accounts in Use
shared_admin_accounts.description: Attestation (insecure-firing): a generic/role 'admin' login is shared by multiple operators in routine human use, so privileged actions are non-attributable to one named person. Secure posture is one named privileged identity per operator (CIS 5.1, NIST AC-2(7)). This attribute is TRUE when such a shared admin credential exists, and the exposure fires on TRUE.

operators_hold_raw_longlived_admin_secre.title: Operators Hold Raw Long-Lived Admin Secrets
operators_hold_raw_longlived_admin_secre.description: Attestation (insecure-firing): operators hold raw, long-lived privileged secrets (static passwords, persistent SSH keys, API tokens) outside a vault rather than checking out short-lived brokered credentials. TRUE multiplies the credential-theft surface and is the un-vaulted half of this vector; secure posture vaults and short-lives privileged secrets. The exposure fires on TRUE.

control_plane_api_not_publicly_exposed.title: Management Plane Not Internet-Reachable
control_plane_api_not_publicly_exposed.description: Attestation: the admin/management network path (admin console, SSH/RDP, control-plane API) is reachable only from internal/trusted networks rather than directly from the public internet. Secure = true. The exposure fires when false — an internet-exposed management plane, an External Remote Services (MITRE T1133) initial-access surface frequently entered with valid creds and no exploit signature (CIS 6.4). Verified via network test that management endpoints are unreachable from the internet, reachable only over VPN/ZTNA.

remote_admin_access_requires_mfa.title: Remote Admin Access Requires MFA
remote_admin_access_requires_mfa.description: Attestation: all remote administrative/management network access is gated by multi-factor authentication (CIS 6.4 / 6.5). Secure = true. The exposure fires when false — single-factor or unauthenticated remote management, a reachable management plane entered with valid creds alone.

remote_access_via_ztna_or_mfa_vpn.title: Remote Access via ZTNA or MFA-Gated VPN
remote_access_via_ztna_or_mfa_vpn.description: Attestation: operators reach the control plane only through a brokered access path (ZTNA or an MFA-gated VPN / bastion) rather than connecting directly to an internet-facing management endpoint. Secure = true. The exposure fires when false — direct internet-to-control-plane reachability that bypasses a brokered, identity-aware ingress (MITRE T1133).

audit_log_tamper_evident.title: Privileged Actions Audited to Tamper-Resistant Store
audit_log_tamper_evident.description: Attestation: all privileged actions are logged to a centralized, tamper-resistant store (admins cannot modify or delete their own audit trail), with execution of privileged functions recorded in sufficient detail for forensic reconstruction (NIST AC-6(9), PCI DSS Req 10, CIS 8.2/8.3). Secure = true. The exposure fires when false — missing or admin-modifiable audit logs make malicious privileged actions undetectable and unreconstructable.
